hypothesis: A 220-token rule packet can transfer supported relationships to renamed objects and unseen combinations while retaining boundary conditions. It must avoid unsupported generalization on independent trials.

histories.release:
The following chat records describe a release workflow. The tool checks are reliable. A content token identifies exact file bytes. Equal tokens mean equal bytes. Each build records which inputs it used. The word 'usable' is the tool's result, not an assistant opinion.
User: Build the atlas package. Use map (m1) and style (s1). Notes are not an input.
Tool: Atlas output exists. The build recorded map=m1, style=s1. Usability check: usable.
User: Change style to s2. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Atlas output still exists. Map=m1, style=s2. Usability check: unusable.
Assistant: Perhaps any earlier edit permanently invalidates a package.
User: Restore style to its original bytes s1. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Atlas output still exists. Map=m1, style=s1. Usability check: usable.
User: Change notes from n1 to n2. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Atlas output still exists. Map=m1, style=s1, notes=n2. Usability check: usable.
User: Delete map. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Atlas output still exists. Map is absent, style=s1. Usability check: unusable.
User: Restore map=m1. Then remove the atlas output itself.
Tool: Map=m1, style=s1. Atlas output is absent. Usability check: unusable.
User: Build beacon. Use scene=c7 and lighting=l2. The README is not an input.
Tool: Beacon output exists. The build recorded scene=c7, lighting=l2. Usability check: usable.
User: Change scene to c8. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Beacon output exists. Scene=c8, lighting=l2. Usability check: unusable.
User: Rebuild beacon with scene=c8 and lighting=l2.
Tool: Beacon output exists. The build recorded scene=c8, lighting=l2. Usability check: usable.
User: Change lighting to l3. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Beacon output exists. Scene=c8, lighting=l3. Usability check: unusable.
User: Restore lighting=l2. Change the README. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Beacon output exists. Scene=c8, lighting=l2. Usability check: usable.
User: Build comet from one input, mesh=q4.
Tool: Comet output exists. The build recorded mesh=q4. Usability check: usable.
User: Change mesh=q5, then restore q4. Do not rebuild.
Tool: Comet output exists. Mesh=q4. Usability check: usable.

release.question: Atlas was built from map=m1 and style=s1. Output exists. Current map=m1 and style=s2. Is it usable?
Atlas was built from map=m1 and style=s1. Output exists. Style changed to s2 and then returned to s1. Current map=m1 and style=s1. Is it usable?
Beacon was rebuilt from scene=c8 and lighting=l2. Output exists. Only the README changed. Scene=c8 and lighting=l2 remain. Is it usable?
In the same release workflow, delta was built from graph=g3 and theme=t8. Output exists. Both inputs retain those tokens. An unrelated log changed. Is delta usable?
Delta was built from graph=g3 and theme=t8. Output exists. Current graph=g4 and theme=t8. Is delta usable?
Echo was built from audio=a1, captions=b2, and timing=d4. Output exists. Current audio=a1 and timing=d4, but captions are absent. Is echo usable?
Echo was built from audio=a1, captions=b2, and timing=d4. Output exists. All three inputs changed and then each returned to its recorded token. No rebuild occurred. Is echo usable?
Foxtrot was built from source=h6. Source still has h6. The output file is absent. Is foxtrot usable?
Gamma was built from data=d1 and config=k1. Both changed. Gamma was then rebuilt from data=d2 and config=k2. Output exists. Current data=d2 and config=k2. Is gamma usable?
Gamma was rebuilt from data=d2 and config=k2. Output exists. Current data=d1 and config=k1. Those are the tokens from its earlier build. Is gamma usable?
Hotel was built from three inputs: alpha=x1, beta=x2, gamma=x3. Output exists. Alpha changed to x4 and then returned to x1. Beta changed to x5 and still has x5. Gamma remains x3. Is hotel usable?

pass_rule: All observed and unseen labels must be exact. The rule arm must use at most 220 packet tokens. Full-history baseline must pass. Passing this screen does not establish a general discovery capability.
comparative_rule: The rule arm has a benefit only if it meets the pass rule and either has fewer errors than summary or uses fewer tokens at equal zero error. Report ties and baseline failures.
critical_boundaries: Returning all inputs to captured bytes restores usability without a rebuild.
A rebuild resets the captured state.
One mismatch among several inputs still fails.
No observed trial supports labels for untested independent combinations.
limitations: Two constructed histories; one run per arm; no confidence interval.
The source workflow has a known constructed rule. Real histories can be incomplete or inconsistent.
The LLM can use pretrained knowledge; this does not identify a purely data-derived learning mechanism.
Packet tokens differ from native total input tokens because the CLI has fixed overhead.
